arguments: Unvalidated data and output vector pointers are forwarded to PSA hash routines
message.text: Unvalidated data and output vector pointers are forwarded to PSA hash routines

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: valid because the shim copies caller-supplied vector bases and lengths directly into psa_hash_compute, while the resolved PSA implementation only uses assertions for required non-NULL/nonzero output parameters and returns success before touching output when input_length is zero. Evidence: secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_hash.c:112-118 forwards in_vec[1].base/len and out_vec[0].base/len plus &out_vec[0].len without local checks, and lib/ext/thin-psa-crypto-core/thin_psa_crypto_core.c:398-407 shows psa_hash_compute returns PSA_SUCCESS for zero input_length then otherwise relies on assert(input/hash/hash_size/hash_length) before the driver call. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: Validate vector bases consistently at the shim boundary: require input != NULL when input_length > 0, hash != NULL when hash_size > 0 or when an output is required, and optionally pre-check hash_size against PSA_HASH_LENGTH(iov->alg) for supported algorithms before calling psa_hash_compute.
properties.reasoning: For the single-part hash compute operation, this shim forwards caller-controlled in_vec[1].base and out_vec[0].base to psa_hash_compute without checking that a nonzero input length has a non-NULL input pointer, or that the output vector is non-NULL and large enough for a hash result before passing it into the crypto library. PSA APIs generally validate parameters, but this file is the secure service boundary and also passes &out_vec[0].len for the callee to write. If lower layers or configurations assume the IPC layer performed pointer validation, malformed vectors could cause a fault or unintended memory access in secure code.
